title: Kitchen Fitting Cost Wren: What to Budget
description: Kitchen fitting cost with Wren explained: what installation includes, possible extra charges and when an independent kitchen fitter may offer better value.

blocks.text: If you are comparing kitchen suppliers, the kitchen fitting cost with Wren may be as important as the price of the cabinets and worktops. Check whether the supplier's quotation separates the kitchen supply from installation, and review exactly what is included. The final fitting cost can depend on the size and shape of the room, the number of units, your chosen appliances and any work needed before installation. There is no single price that applies to every kitchen project, so treat any fitting figure as a project-specific estimate rather than a standard rate.
How much does Wren kitchen fitting cost?

Ask Wren for a current installation quotation based on your design and the work identified for your room. Costs can be affected by whether you are replacing an existing kitchen in the same layout or moving sinks, appliances and services. A simple installation with sound walls, level floors and little alteration is usually less involved than a full kitchen renovation requiring plumbing, electrical work, plastering, flooring or tiling. As a rough guide, UK kitchen fitting and associated installation work can typically cost several thousand pounds, depending on the scope. Every project differs, so obtain a free, no-obligation quote for accurate pricing. Check separately whether units, appliances, worktops and accessories are included in any installation figure.

The exact scope should be confirmed in writing. Kitchen installation may involve assembling and securing cabinets, fitting doors and drawers, installing worktops and connecting appliances or sinks where agreed. Removal of an old kitchen may be available as an additional service. Plumbing, electrical and finishing work can be included, excluded or separately priced depending on the quotation. Do not assume that every task needed to make the room fully usable is included simply because the quotation is described as kitchen fitting.

items: Fitting doors, drawers, handles, plinths and panels.
Worktop installation, subject to the material and agreed fitting method.
Connection of appliances or sinks where included in the written scope.
Removal of existing units, flooring or waste only when specifically priced.
Making good, decorating, tiling and flooring, which may be included or charged separately.

blocks.text: Potential extra charges to check before agreeing

Preparation work identified after the old kitchen is removed can add labour and material costs. Uneven floors, damp, damaged plaster, unsuitable walls or outdated services may need attention before fitting can continue. Moving a sink, dishwasher, cooker or washing machine can require changes to plumbing or electrical routes. A new layout may also require plastering, flooring, tiling, lighting or decorating. Ask for likely exclusions and how any additional work will be approved before it starts.

items: Removing and disposing of the old kitchen, appliances or rubble.
Moving or upgrading plumbing, waste pipes and electrical points.
Gas-related work, where applicable, carried out by an appropriately qualified professional.
Extra worktops, upstands, end panels, filler panels or decorative pieces.
Cut-outs, joins and specialist installation for stone, quartz or other demanding worktop materials.
Floor levelling, new flooring, wall repairs, plastering, tiling and painting.
Alterations caused by missing, damaged or incorrect components.
Additional visits or labour if the room, services or delivered items are not ready.

blocks.text: Questions to ask about a Wren installation quotation

Before comparing a Wren fitting cost with an independent quote, ask for an itemised breakdown. Check whether VAT is included, what happens to the old kitchen, who removes packaging and waste, and whether appliance connections are covered. Ask how damaged or missing parts will be handled and whether the installation price can change if extra work is identified. It is also worth confirming the expected start date, estimated duration, payment stages and what you must arrange before the fitting team arrives. A low headline figure can be misleading if essential preparation is excluded.
When might an independent kitchen fitter offer better value?

An independent fitter may offer better value when you want a more flexible scope of work or when the kitchen needs substantial alterations. You can compare detailed quotes and choose a contractor able to coordinate cabinet fitting with plumbing, electrics, tiling, flooring and decorating. This can be useful if you are not buying every component from one supplier, want to retain existing appliances or are combining a kitchen replacement with wider renovation work. The clarity of a quotation depends on the individual contractor, so compare the scope, labour, materials and preparation work carefully.

The lowest independent quote is not automatically the best option. Confirm who will carry out each trade, whether waste removal is included, how variations are approved and what happens if a problem is found. Check that the fitter understands the installation requirements for your chosen cabinets, worktops and appliances. Comparing Wren with a local renovation team

A supplier installation package may suit homeowners who want the kitchen supply and fitting considered together. A local renovation company may be more suitable where the project involves a layout change, structural preparation or several finishing trades. The most useful comparison is a like-for-like schedule of work. List the cabinets, worktops, appliances, removal, plumbing, electrics, lighting, flooring, tiling, decorating, waste disposal and making good. Then mark each item as included, excluded or provisional. This can show whether a fitting cost is lower because important parts of the renovation have been left for you to organise. It also helps you plan a clearer budget before ordering materials or committing to a start date.

faq.q: Does Wren kitchen price include fitting?
faq.a: This depends on Wren's current quotation and the package you select. Check whether kitchen supply and installation are listed separately, and ask for an itemised scope of work.

faq.q: What extra costs can come with Wren kitchen installation?
faq.a: Possible additional costs can include removal and disposal, plumbing or electrical alterations, flooring, tiling, plastering, decorating, worktop changes and repairs identified after the old kitchen is removed. Confirm exclusions in writing.

faq.q: Is it cheaper to use an independent kitchen fitter than Wren?
faq.a: There is no universal saving. An independent fitter may be useful where you need flexible work or several renovation trades, but compare like-for-like written quotes and confirm exactly what each includes.

faq.q: How can I compare a Wren fitting quote with another quote?
faq.a: Request an itemised breakdown covering labour, materials, removal, appliances, services, finishing work, waste and VAT. Make sure both quotations cover the same kitchen components and preparation work.
